card.name: Linking words before enzyme inhibitor/inducer terms
card.fires_on: Small words like "are", "or" and "moderate" that come right before a descriptor of enzyme activity or metabolizer status (strong inducers, poor metabolizers, weak inhibitors). Seen in drug-interaction sections.

modes.label: "are" after drugs that
modes.description: The verb "are" after "drugs that" or a drug name, just before inducer or inhibitor wording.
modes.example: Drugs that<< are>> strong inducers of UGT1A

modes.label: "or" between metabolizer types
modes.description: "or" joining intermediate and poor metabolizers of a CYP enzyme.
modes.example: especially in transplant patients who are intermediate<< or>> poor metabolizers of CYP

modes.label: Strength word before inhibitor
modes.description: A strength word such as "moderate" placed before the word inhibitor.
modes.example: Abiraterone is a CYP2D6<< moderate>> inhibitor.

card.writes: It promotes Chinese words meaning good or strong (as in "a good ..."), which fits predicting a grade or quality descriptor next; this is a weak, mismatched effect.
card.plain: It fires on the small linking word just before a drug is described as a strong, moderate or weak enzyme inducer or inhibitor.
